1. Case 1: Psoriatic arthritis (nail), Pustules under fingernails with swollen DIP joints and dystrophic nails suggest inflammatory erosive arthropathy. Hand radiography showing phalangeal erosions supports psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement. Negative cultures/serologies and antibiotic failure reduce infectious/reactive mimics. Retinoid/methotrexate use and worsening favor immune-mediated disease. Thus psoriatic arthritis with nail involvement is most likely; other hypotheses are less likely.

Case 2: Leukemic orbital/CNS relapse, The patient's prior ALL with repeated CNS relapses and current bilateral proptosis, blurred vision, headache, and optic disc swelling initially pointed toward leukemic relapse. New imaging demonstrating progressive orbital roof scalloping and medial wall displacement indicates orbital leukemic infiltration, while a CSF blast count of 1400×10^6/L with elevated opening pressure confirms leptomeningeal involvement. These findings directly support the leukemic relapse hypothesis and refute IIH, since the elevated CSF pressure is explained by meningeal leukemic infiltration rather than primary idiopathic intracranial hypertension. Orbital pseudotumor/infection is also excluded by the destructive bony changes and CSF blasts. With strong supporting evidence and no refuting evidence, the diagnosis is confidently established as leukemic orbital/CNS relapse.

Skin biopsy showed vacuolar interface dermatitis with lymphohistiocytic infiltrate and pigment incontinence, with no malignant cells; both pathologist and laboratory physician interpreted this as consistent with immune-related skin toxicity. The temporal relationship with nivolumab, pruritic papules/plaques, and biopsy findings strongly support this diagnosis (confidence 0.88).
